title: Semiconductors and SOI: From Bulk Wafers to Engineered Substrates
gist: Tutorial on why engineered substrates (SOI) displaced bulk silicon for specialty uses: Smart Cut (CEA-Leti 1991, Soitec 1992) made SOI manufacturable, but cost, self-heating and a limited scaling path kept it a specialty platform as leading-edge logic chose FinFET/GAA. SOI owns smartphone RF front-ends, Photonics-SOI (>$100m at Soitec, CPO ramp) is the fastest-growing segment, and FD-SOI is heading sub-10 nm (GF FDX Fusion, production 2028), while Soitec's FY26 revenue fell 34% on RF-SOI destocking.

insights.claim: From the 1990s, parasitics, leakage and isolation problems rooted in the shared conductive bulk-silicon substrate began limiting speed, power and RF performance, and by 180–130 nm these effects were costing speed and power at each node, prompting engineered substrates like SOI.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Explains the structural demand for engineered substrates as a specialty wafer market.

insights.claim: Bulk CMOS drawbacks include junction capacitance, latch-up, short-channel effects, random dopant fluctuation, leakage, radiation sensitivity, substrate noise/RF loss and lack of true dielectric isolation, all traced to the conductive substrate.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Each drawback maps to an SOI end market (RF, rad-hard, low-power).

insights.claim: Smart Cut, invented by Michel Bruel at CEA-Leti in 1991 and industrialized by spin-out Soitec from 1992, uses a hydrogen implant to define a cleave plane, enabling film thickness control within a few ångströms across 300 mm and became the industry-standard SOI process.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Soitec's IP and process know-how underpin its dominant SOI position.

insights.claim: FD-SOI uses a ~5–7 nm silicon film over a ~20–25 nm buried oxide, giving full gate control without channel doping, and has shipped at 28 nm (ST, Samsung 28FDS), 22 nm (GF 22FDX) and 18 nm (ST/Samsung 18FDS), with GF 12FDX next.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Identifies the FD-SOI foundry ecosystem and node roadmap.

insights.claim: FD-SOI back-biasing shifts threshold voltage by roughly 60–85 mV per volt, letting the same silicon be tuned after fabrication per block and dynamically for speed or leakage — something bulk FinFETs cannot do to any useful degree.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Key differentiator for low-power edge, IoT and automotive designs.
insights.quote: The same silicon can be tuned after fabrication, per block and dynamically, which bulk FinFETs cannot do to any useful degree.

insights.claim: RF-SOI with a high-resistivity handle and trap-rich layer is used in antenna switches, LNAs and tuners in virtually every smartphone front-end, while Photonics-SOI underpins silicon photonics, pluggable transceivers and co-packaged optics.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: SOI demand is tied to smartphone RF and AI optical interconnect cycles.

themes.theme: Why SOI stayed a specialty platform

insights.claim: SOI wafers cost several times a bulk prime wafer; FD-SOI proponents argue planar processing saves masks versus FinFET, but the die-cost comparison depends on node and volume.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Wafer cost premium limits SOI's addressable logic market.

insights.claim: The buried oxide conducts heat about 100 times worse than silicon, causing SOI self-heating that degrades mobility and reliability, and below about 10 nm FD-SOI films would need to be under 5 nm, which is why leading-edge logic chose FinFET and gate-all-around nanosheets.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: SOI is unlikely to re-enter leading-edge logic; its growth is in specialty segments.

insights.claim: The thin-SOI wafer market is concentrated in one supplier, creating a single-source risk customers weigh; market-research firms commonly put Soitec's SOI wafer share well above half.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Soitec has pricing power but customers may push for second sources (SEH, Simgui).
insights.quote: one wafer supplier holds most of the thin-SOI market, a single-source risk customers weigh

insights.claim: Soitec's fiscal 2026 (Apr 2025–Mar 2026) revenue was €592m, down 34%, with Mobile Communications revenue falling 41% at constant currency on customer RF-SOI destocking.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Soitec is highly exposed to smartphone inventory cycles; watch RF-SOI destocking normalization.

insights.claim: Soitec reports Photonics-SOI revenue above $100m in FY26 with co-packaged optics qualification volumes in preparation for ramp-up, making it currently the fastest-growing SOI segment as AI data centers need 800G–1.6T optical links.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: AI optical interconnect is Soitec's main growth offset to the RF-SOI downturn.

insights.claim: Soitec impaired €41m of SmartSiC assets in FY26 as the EV slowdown delayed its bonded SiC-substrate effort, while its POI piezoelectric substrate won a multi-year supply agreement with Skyworks in March 2026.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Mixed diversification: SiC weak with EVs, POI/5G filters supported by Skyworks deal.

insights.claim: SOI wafer supply includes Shin-Etsu Handotai (second SOI source for major foundries), SUMCO and GlobalWafers with smaller shares, and China's Simgui, a Soitec licensee whose license framework was extended 10 years in March 2026.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: China localization of SOI via Simgui could erode Soitec share over time.

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries is the largest FD-SOI foundry (22FDX, 12FDX, Dresden/Malta/Singapore), STMicroelectronics runs 28/18 nm FD-SOI with embedded PCM including the STM32V8 used on SpaceX's Starlink, and Samsung Foundry offers 28FDS/18FDS with eMRAM as ST's second source.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: FD-SOI is anchored by European capacity and ST/GF/Samsung platforms.

insights.claim: On 9 Oct 2026 GlobalFoundries announced FDX Fusion, an FD-SOI platform targeting 7 nm-class digital performance with over twice first-gen FDX density, with demonstrators in early 2027, first PDK mid-2027 and Dresden production in 2028.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Timeline milestones to track for GF's edge-AI positioning.

insights.claim: FD-SOI's pitch is performance per watt with RF and memory on one die rather than peak speed — the profile of sensor fusion, robotics and radar — and embedded PCM (ST) and eMRAM (Samsung) replace embedded flash, which does not scale below 28 nm.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Physical/edge AI and automotive MCUs are FD-SOI's growth markets.
insights.quote: FD-SOI’s pitch is not peak speed but performance per watt with RF and memory on one die

insights.claim: Layer transfer, wafer bonding and backside processing — core Smart Cut skills — are now central to 3D integration, backside power delivery and hybrid bonding in leading-edge logic even where the chip is not SOI.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Substrate-engineering know-how gains relevance in advanced packaging and leading-edge logic.
insights.quote: Even where the final chip is not SOI, the substrate-engineering know-how is.

insights.claim: Key open questions for SOI are whether FDX Fusion and 10 nm FD-SOI win enough volume against 3 nm-class GAA for edge AI, when RF-SOI inventories normalize, and whether Chinese SOI supply such as Simgui gains share as local foundries adopt FD-SOI.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Defines the watchlist for Soitec and FD-SOI foundry theses.
